title: Ran out of gas: what to do
metaDesc: Ran out of gas? Hazard lights on, coast off the road, stay buckled inside if it's safe, and call roadside help for fuel. Don't walk along a highway.
first: When the engine sputters or dies, turn on your hazard lights and coast as far right, off the road, as you can.
Steering and brakes get heavier with the engine off. Hold the wheel firmly and press the brake hard and steady.
Once stopped, if you're safely off the road, stay inside with your seat belt on.
Call roadside help and ask for fuel delivery.
If you're stuck in a traffic lane, call 911.
dont: Don't walk along a highway to get gas.
Never try to cross a road with moving traffic.
Don't stand between your car and traffic.

steps.t: Head for the nearest gas station. How far you can still go varies a lot from car to car, so don't count on it.

steps.h: If you have to get out
steps.t: Get out on the side away from traffic. Wait behind a guardrail if there is one, at least 40 feet from the car.

call: Call your roadside plan or your insurer's roadside line for fuel delivery or a tow.
Call 911 if you're stuck in a traffic lane or you feel unsafe.

sources.t: AAA Club Alliance: Staying safe when your car breaks down
